definitions.explanation: A waste sorting category in Japan for items that cannot be incinerated, such as metals, ceramics, glass, and certain plastics. Collection days and accepted items vary by municipality.

examples.japanese: {燃|も}えないゴミは{水曜日|すいようび}に{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Non-burnable trash goes out on Wednesdays.

examples.japanese: フライパンは{燃|も}えないゴミに{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: A frying pan is classified as non-burnable trash.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{時|とき}、{燃|も}えないゴミの{出|だ}し{方|かた}が{分|わ}からなくて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: When I moved, I had trouble figuring out how to dispose of non-burnable trash.

notes:
An essential term for daily life in Japan. Japanese waste sorting (ゴミの{分別|ぶんべつ}) is strict and varies by municipality. Residents must separate trash into categories and put each type out on the designated collection day.

MAIN TRASH CATEGORIES:
- {燃|も}えるゴミ / {可燃|かねん}ゴミ: burnable trash (food waste, paper, wood)
- {燃|も}えないゴミ / {不燃|ふねん}ゴミ: non-burnable trash (metal, glass, ceramics)
- {資源|しげん}ゴミ: recyclable waste (bottles, cans, PET bottles, newspapers)
- {粗大|そだい}ゴミ: oversized/bulky trash (furniture, appliances)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {燃|も}えないゴミを{出|だ}す: to put out non-burnable trash
- {燃|も}えないゴミの{日|ひ}: non-burnable trash collection day
- {燃|も}えないゴミの{袋|ふくろ}: non-burnable trash bag

ALTERNATE FORMS:
- {不燃|ふねん}ゴミ: non-combustible waste — the more formal equivalent used on official signs and in municipal documents
